The broadcast originates in [server/events/sse.go](/app/server/events/sse.go:80): `SendMessage` receives no request context, and the broker queues every event for every subscriber. Subscribers also have no client unique ID to compare with the sender.

The fix needs a per-window UUID sent by [httpClient.js](/app/ui/src/dataProvider/httpClient.js:8), header and cookie middleware registered before the loggers in [server.go](/app/server/server.go:56), and context helpers in [request.go](/app/model/request/request.go:11). The SSE connection uses `EventSource`, which cannot set a custom header; its preceding keepalive request can establish the cookie. Delivery filtering then belongs in the broker, with request contexts passed from [media_annotation.go](/app/server/subsonic/media_annotation.go:77) and the intended broadcast contexts chosen in [scanner.go](/app/scanner/scanner.go:101).

One integration detail needs care: native API authentication stores `User` in context, while Subsonic also stores `Username`. Filtering must use the authenticated username for both paths.

I inspected code and existing tests and recorded the findings in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). I did not edit project source or tests because my assigned role is fault localization only, so the issue remains unresolved.

Implemented selective SSE delivery. The UI now sends a per-window client UUID on API and login requests; middleware stores it in an HttpOnly cookie and request context. The broker uses that context to skip the originating client and deliver user-action events only to other sessions of the same user. Server-originated events still broadcast.

Updated event call sites, the diode API, and cookie expiry constants. Focused delivery and middleware tests pass, as do the affected Go packages, UI formatting check, and `git diff --check`.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** The UI gives each tab a UUID, but [eventStream.js](/app/ui/src/eventStream.js:17) opens `EventSource` without it. The server instead reads a browser-wide cookie for that request ([middlewares.go](/app/server/middlewares.go:63)). If another tab updates the cookie before the stream opens or reconnects, the subscription gets the wrong client ID. An action can then echo to its originating tab or be withheld from the other tab. Bind the SSE subscription to its tab’s UUID, for example by passing the UUID in the stream URL and resolving it when subscribing.

**Tests:** `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./server/events ./server ./server/subsonic ./scanner ./model/request` passed; `CI=true npm test -- --watch=false --runInBand` passed (11 suites, 41 tests); `git diff --check` passed. No `TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM`. Project code was not changed during this independent review.

Fixed the SSE tab identification issue. The UI now includes its per-tab UUID in the stream URL, and the server uses that ID for the subscription even if another tab has changed the shared cookie. A regression test covers the mismatch and confirms that the originating tab does not receive its own event.

The reviewer’s exact Go and UI test commands passed, as did `git diff --check`. No failures remain.
